steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You know... before I came to Rhodes Island, I'd already anticipated a lot of what I'd encounter. But it only dawned on me, once it all actually came, how none of my preparation was any use.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Being military—even if I was just the most minor guard of honor—I'd always believed firmly in the tenacity of life, that it shouldn't slip away so easily.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: But in this past year, traveling all over Terra's parts with this ship, I've witnessed far too many people...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Too many people who part like an unnoticed gust of wind, gone gently far before you even notice they came by.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Unable to leave something behind.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I try and make a record of their faces, their lives that passed on before me, but in just one short year, they've managed to vanish from my memory too.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You've been through all that yourself, right?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: But you won't give me the answers, will you?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Look at me, still acting like I used to, going through everything on my mind and dumping it on you.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I brought some flowers today, but they're a little wilted. There weren't any convoys willing to come to these parts, so I just had to walk, and it's hard to keep a bouquet fresh all the way.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: (Is someone there...?)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sorry, Lass. Please wait a moment, if you can.
It's you. Jane Willow.
How come you're...?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: How do you know my name?
D-Don't kill me!
I'm Acton! Acton Corsaire! 5th Defence, 6th Camp of the County Hillock Barracks. D-Do you remember me? We met, just a few years ago!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Yes. I remember, I've met you before. What are you doing here? Haven't the troops here long withdrawn from their stations?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: (He pulls on his sleeve.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Your arm... You weren't able to evacuate from District Seventeen?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Not one of us had any order to retreat from above when the dirty bombs came. Maybe our kit was broken, or the commanders forgot, or maybe...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Heh—the farmers know it best, don't they? It's hard not to mess up a few wheat buds when you pull weeds.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm so sorry, Acton.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: No, it's fine. I'm more wondering, Jane, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I... I'm back here to grieve over someone lost.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: What about you? Do you just live in these ruins?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: No, our camp's in the rough outside the plate, I was just in the ruins looking for food. I never thought I'd run into you.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: So you mean, there's other people living here, aside from you?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Yeah. On top of the soldiers who got left behind, there's a few Taran survivors drifting around here.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: After the events, the Army wanted to round up the surviving Infected and keep them under control in one place, so they organized a few searches, but we were lucky enough to avoid those.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Then later down the line, the ruin and pollution here got too severe for their tastes, so they decided to completely abandon this plate, and leave anyone on it to fend for themselves.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Then... did you find anything earlier?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: (Shakes head.) Hah. Going hungry for another few days, looks like.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I've got some rations and medication on me. If you want it, you can have them all.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Thank you, Janie.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Do you have a transmitter here? If I can get in touch with my colleagues, they might be willing to send some supplies in for us.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Er, I've seen one in the ruins.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Where?!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Not far, but it's where the Tarans are active... If the two of us run into them, it'll get very tricky.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Both sides might be on the same raft, but everyone has it tough. We don't want to feed any more conflict.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: So usually, as long as we can... we try and keep away from each other as much as possible.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton, show me the way at least. I need to try, no matter what.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: The active Originium's already concentrated above safe limits ahead... Is this really what the Tarans are living in?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I've been walking for so long... without a person in sight.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wait, is that someone?!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Ma'am! Hold on, please!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I don't mean any harm!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I have some emergency pharmaceuticals and rations here! In exchange, would you let me use the transmitter?!

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Are...

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Are you telling... the truth? You have medicine?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I do. Here, look, you can take it all if you need.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Come with me.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Aislinn, I'm here, I brought somebody.

steps.name: Dying Girl
steps.text: Hurts... help me.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: This is my girl. Can your medicine save her?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I... Her condition's too severe. It'd be tricky for emergency drugs to take effect.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Try, please. She's not even seven...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'll... do everything I can.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Aislinn, can you hear what I'm saying?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: (She administers an injection into the girl's body.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It'll be okay, don't fret.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: How is she?!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm sorry, it's just... not any use.

steps.name: Dying Girl
steps.text: It's dark... Mam, I'm... scared.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Aislinn, Aislinn, don't be afraid, Mam's right here with you.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I just... don't have anything I can do. I'm so sorry, ma'am.

steps.name: Dying Girl
steps.text: It's cold...

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: (Hugs the girl tight.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Ma'am...

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: Just go. Don't come back here.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'll leave this food.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm staying in the rough outside the plate for the next few days. If any of you need help, you can come ask me.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sorry to bother you. I'll be gone in a moment.

steps.name: Feeble Woman
steps.text: The stuff you want to use is in the building opposite. You can move it on your own.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Hey, steady there!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Huff—it didn't occur to me how far your camp would be from the plate.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'm surprised you brought back something so massive all by yourself!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Okay, okay, no time to wallow now, Acton. Let's see if it still works at all first.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Here's the screwdriver.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Oh, we're in luck. It's all intact inside. Just a little adjustment, and it'll be in service.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: You know your way around these things too? I'm blown away... When did you learn this?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: All I can say is, I've picked up a heck of a lot from my new job. Alright, here's your screwdriver back, thanks.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'll go hook up the generator.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: How is it? Lights on?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Yep, it's on without a hitch.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: How did you find this device? Did the Taran group give you trouble?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No, I traded with them for the supplies I had on me.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: That's good, then. At least they know a deal's a deal.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: We need to hold on for a very long while before the supplies arrive.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: During this period, I'd like to start up a few fields, plant some crops and ensure food self-sufficiency. It beats searching the plate by a mile, with how inefficient that is, not to mention the danger.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: That's all well and good, but... a lot of the camp are stuck in dire days. We have barely any proper manpower.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: There's the displaced Tarans aboard the plate too. I'd like them to join in... If we can provide food and clean water, I don't think they'd refuse.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: That's not happening. The first thing that bunch did was drive the lot of us out!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton, I know the rift is intense between your two sides, and making peace seems unimaginable, but this is a dire situation. None of you have any other choice.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I can only offer you temporary aid. After that, carrying on all comes down to you, and the only ones left who can join hands with you and push on are them. Fellow Infected of yours.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: So, either you shelve your grudge for the time being, and together you survive, or you hold onto your hate, and together you die here.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Let me think... I need to ask the others.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton, I met a woman while I was looking for the transmitter... I wasn't able to save her daughter's life, but she still pointed me the right way.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: The woman with the child? I know her. No wonder... She's the only one I've seen in the past few days.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: *sigh* I can't imagine what she does now... her husband, father and sister, they all left her in that atrocity, and now... even her daughter's gone.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: So give it a think, Acton. They're just a group of people that want to survive, same as you.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Hey, Chuck, d'you trust these people? I just feel like they'd have to have something in store for us down the line.

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: Don't know, nor do I want to. Haven't had a meal for days. Brain just says, eat something to keep the needle off empty.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: It's some swindle, absolutely. I tell you, these army boys, they've got hell in mind for us.

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: So what? You keep talking, but here you are anyway.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Hmph... that Vouivre's holding onto Oripathy suppressants there. My bad parts have been feeling like murder in recent days.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: There's simple water purifiers on the camp's east. To the south is the farmland we're about to clear. The sick have all agreed to be housed for nursing in the tent on the north end.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: At noontime and evening each day, you can get a portion of food from the center of the camp.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Ahem... that's all. Janie, anything you'd like to add?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Can I just ask everyone, have you seen a woman around? She's very slim, and she's carrying a girl... but the child passed away not long ago.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Máire? You mean Máire?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Brown hair, small mole under her eyes?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Right, that's her. What do you want with her? What, has she offended you?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No, I just wanted to ask, is she doing okay?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Mystery, isn't it? Haven't seen her who knows how long. Could be dead herself in someplace.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: But you... I thought you would've at least been aware of each other.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Here?!

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Vouivre, no one's got the time to care for anyone else here.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: What are you looking at me like that for? I'm just... telling the truth.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It's fine. Thank you all for coming out so far. Get some rest as soon as you can. We have a lot of things waiting for us tomorrow.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Janie, I don't understand. Where's the point in what you're doing? We've given them food to eat, and a place to stay.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'm not crossing my fingers they'll be happy with us any day, but at the very least, we could just about live without bothering each other!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Take yesterday, I heard a brawl sprung up while work was happening, and someone's still lying on the couch today with stars around their head.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Ungh... this fruit's too high. I can't reach.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Janie, Janie! Are you listening to me?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Hm? Oh, that, I know. It was one of yours who decided to be rude first, Acton.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Says who?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I rushed over the moment the conflict sparked off, and it was me who helped the one with a knock on the head back to camp too.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: The... Did you even sort out what happened, Janie?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I did. So, as a token of apology, I think you can present them this basket of fruit, in person.

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: This is killing me... Miss Saileach, am I going to die?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You'll be fine, I've already jabbed you with painkillers. Just hold on a little, and it'll kick in soon.

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Thank you... *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: How are you now? Any better?

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: If you could just, keep talking to me... I'm scared.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: What do you want to hear?

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Anything, I just want... to have a voice by my side.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Alright. Will a song be okay?

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: 'If only we were a pair of white feathers, roaming free on the breaks of the waves,'

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: 'Time would farewell us to be forgotten, and never would either we sorrow again...'

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: Miss Saileach...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Shh, he's asleep.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: (Thank you, Mr. Chuck, for being so willing to help me look after these people.)

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: (No problem. Want some wild fruit? I'll fetch you one.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: (Wild fruit? Did you pick it?)

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: (No, it's from an army boy. They taste alright. Don't know why they felt so kind all of a sudden.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: (I'm guessing, they wanted to apologize for what happened a few days ago.)

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: (That's a tall tale...)

steps.name: Pained Sickly Soldier
steps.text: Rgh... cold.
Though his face twists as he does it, the man tucks the patient gently back into his bed.

steps.name: Apathetic Taran Man
steps.text: (Tch. Boy can't even sleep tight.)

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Acton, quickly, wake up!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What is it, Janie?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: There's a serious leak in the north side patients' tent! Fetch a few people to come with me, quickly!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What?! Hold on, I'll be right there.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Quickly, Acton!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'm here. How are the sick inside? What's your plan? Dammit, the rain must have ruined these boys' conditions. What the hell do we do now?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: The Tarans came over first thing. I suppose they've moved them to other tents by now.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I said, the Tarans made it in time to move the patients out! They're all safe!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Including ours?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Yes, including the soldiers, but they weren't in time to shift the pharmaceuticals I brought. I'm afraid those are all soaked now.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: That's fine, I'll think of something.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Thank you, Deaglán, for coming with me to find Acton.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Thank those drugs you've got, not me.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Actually, I ran out of my medicine. The stuff we've been handing out to everyone over the last few days, that was all stuff Acton found with a few others by braving the ruins...

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Tch. Some shite.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Oi, Acton! The hell are you, you bleeding moron? Will you give us a shout already!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'm... I'm over here, I got trapped.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Are you hurt?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: No, it was just, the exit collapsed...

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: What got you inside this cellar, anyway?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Enough of that, give me a hand. There's an injured woman here who's out cold.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Alright, I'll pull her up.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: It's Máire... She's still alive?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Hey, you want a scone?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: A scone? Are you having a laugh? Where'd you get the stuff to make that?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: It was Janie who whipped it up. I don't know what she went into the forest to pick yesterday, but whatever it was, it let her actually make these.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: No joke? Pass me it, I'll try one.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Who knew I'd ever be sitting here having nibbles? We used to not even have a bite to eat.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: That girl led us through cultivating, raising fowls and treating the sick just fine, and she can even knock together a wood house. We're sitting here now and she's even rustled up desserts.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Eat yours, chop-chop! Want another?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: No, I'll save one for Máire.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: How is she?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Looking a lot better, but she still doesn't talk. Too much of a shock to her, losing her child.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Bless Janie, really. She's been sitting by her side the whole time as of late.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Heh, speaking of. Here she comes.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mr. Acton! I got a reply from my colleagues!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Janie! That's smashing news.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Phew... They were notifying us just now to say, the branch office south is making an urgent partial transfer of their supplies to us.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: When will they arrive?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: If all goes well, in about a week.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: That's lightning fast!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Don't get too excited. I think, based on what they said, the convoy's run into a little issue over there? They say they can't get a precise pin on our position. Something must be funny with the signal...

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: That's fine, I'll head up to the plate in a sec to look. Might find some boosters.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Thank you so much. Another thing, we need to stand a flag in the middle of the camp to serve as a marker. That plus the locator will make it convenient for the convoy to accurately orientate once they're approaching.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: A flag? It's not a tricky problem, is it? We can just tear some bright cloth and hoist it up.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: We need a design, at least.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: If you want a design, you may as well grab one of the old county banners from up on the plate.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: What? You're not going to treat yourself as one of County Hillock, are you?

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Hmph, could use your barracks boys' ensign as well. Might find one of those on the plate too.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Enough... I never want to see that bloody thing for the rest of my life.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Fine... you come up with something, then.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Janie, do you have any ideas?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm not sure myself. We'd have to see what everyone thinks.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: Hmph. Here's what everyone thinks: whatever you think, that's best.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Yeah... I'm in agreement.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sorry, Acton, for making you do sewing work with me at such a late hour.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: That's fine. As long as you don't find me too clumsy.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Not still worrying over the flag there, are you? You look vexed.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I went all around the camp today asking about the flag, but people all seemed to have the same response ready when I did. They want me to decide.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: It's true. Everyone's always had faith in your decisions.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It just makes it harder. I need to come up with a proposal that'll satisfy everyone, or else I'll let you all down for trusting in me.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Janie, you know, even if you turned out a blank white flag, none of us would object.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: All this time, you've been busy like mad for us, leading us onto the plate and into the forest to find food while the sun's not even up.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: You barely rest even when you make it back to camp, what with a million sorts of things needing your handling.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I think, fundamentally, everyone's left this flag to you so that you can catch your breath, take your time sewing and properly unwind.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Really...?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Really. If you kept wracking yourself over this flag, well, that would never do.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: I'll leave the rest of it to you, then, Janie. And I think you've earned an early sleep.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: The candlelight's... a little dim. I'll open the window wider, let the moons come in easier.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Oh! Acton, do you hear that singing?

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It might not be too clear with how the wind's picked up. Listen, carefully.

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Oh, I hear it. Where's it coming from?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I don't know...
A lone, tender song floats through the breeze, trembling and shaking, but having caught it, they begin, unconsciously, to sing along with it.
And the singing gradually rises, and the wind fades. Until, in every corner of the camp, hovers the song.

a.text: ♪ Far in a blink are we from the roses, lilies and stardust all eaten away ♪
♪ And so's though we were a pair of white fowls, sitting atop of the breaks of the waves ♪

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: It's Máire... I heard her murmuring while I was tending to her.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It's beautiful.

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: *yawn*... I need my sleep, what's going on out here? Noise and all...

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: Deaglán! Come over here, quick!

steps.name: Twitchy Taran Man
steps.text: What happened?!

steps.name: Injured Soldier
steps.text: It's Janie! It's Janie!
Squeezing through the crowd, the man looks to the clearing in the camp.
There, meeting the morning dew and biting winds as she faces a flagpole, stands the figure of a girl tall and straight in respect.
Her dress is in order, not a hair out of place, and she holds in her hands a rolled-up flag.

a.text: ♪ If only we were a pair of white feathers, roaming free on the breaks of the waves ♪
♪ Time would farewell us to be forgotten, and never would either we sorrow again ♪
♪ Far in a blink are we from the roses, lilies and stardust all eaten away ♪
♪ And so's though we were a pair of white fowls, sitting atop of the breaks of the waves ♪

steps.text: Following in the girl's song and her hoisting of the halyard, the flag ascends slowly to the sky, where the wind unfurls it.
A pair of white fowlbeasts soar upon it.
